rationale: Three peripherals in different rooms (door_back, motion_living, win_bed) went offline simultaneously while the base station itself is online with normal uplink and storage. The base station log shows E-610 (sub-GHz radio module self-test warning), and the KB states E-610 with multiple simultaneous peripheral drops must always be escalated to FAE. Firmware compatibility is fine (v3 supported) and two of the three devices have healthy batteries (71%, 66%), ruling out a battery or firmware cause for the batch drop. The door_back 8% battery is a coincidental separate issue, not the cause of the simultaneous outage.

complaint: The back door sensor shows a low battery and has gone offline, so I'll change the battery tonight. While I have you on the line, is there anything else I should check? I haven't looked at the rest of the system today, I've been at work.
usability_reason: The response is polite and provides a clear summary, but it is not actionable for the customer's actual question and it makes claims not supported by the session record. The customer asked what else to check and said they had not inspected the system; the record shows no questions asked and no actions performed. Yet the response asserts specific diagnostics (E-610 log, three peripherals offline, battery levels, firmware compatibility) as if checks were completed, and tells the customer no action is needed while ignoring their stated plan to change the back door battery. Clarity is decent, but unsupported claims and lack of actionable guidance lower usability.
